daily_brief: A critical cybersecurity emergency dominated headlines Thursday as governments worldwide took websites offline after AI discovered severe vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language powering roughly 70 percent of the web [BBC, Globe and Mail, RFI]. The US NSA urged immediate patching or system shutdown, while Finland, the Netherlands, and Edinburgh Council preemptively disabled public services. In the Middle East, tensions escalated on two fronts: Iran reported seven oil tankers damaged in the Strait of Hormuz overnight [The Hindu, Globe and Mail], the largest single-day toll since the Iran war began in February, while Saudi Arabia confirmed two killed in an airport attack attributed to Houthi militants [BBC]. Diplomatic efforts on Ukraine showed limited progress despite US envoy Steve Witkoff meeting Putin in St. Petersburg; Russia agreed 'in principle' to resume talks but offered only technical-level discussions, and missiles struck Kyiv hours after the announcement [BBC, Le Monde, Al Jazeera]. The International Criminal Court received the EU's Sakharov Prize [France 24], a pointed rebuke to Washington weeks after Trump announced sanctions against the tribunal. Meanwhile, Nigeria confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja [Guardian], raising concerns as the outbreak spreads westward across Africa.

top_stories.headline: Global Websites Go Offline as AI-Discovered PHP Vulnerabilities Trigger Emergency Response
bullets: Critical vulnerabilities discovered by AI in the PHP programming language, which powers approximately 70% of websites globally, prompted governments and organizations to take systems offline

The US National Security Agency urged organizations to patch immediately or take vulnerable systems offline; Finland shut down government web services, the Netherlands took its cybersecurity agency site offline, and the BBC took pages down
PHP developers released an emergency fix Wednesday; cybersecurity firm Wiz called these 'the most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered' by AI
The White House said federal agencies were working with AI labs to speed up fixes; Japan's Prime Minister urged checking all publicly available websites running PHP

top_stories.headline: Seven Oil Tankers Damaged in Strait of Hormuz as Iran-US Tensions Spike
bullets: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy reported seven oil tankers were either attacked or struck naval mines overnight in the Strait of Hormuz
Four tankers caught fire while transferring oil after being targeted; three others were damaged by naval mines
Iran warned it could expand attacks to US bases in the region if Washington continues guiding commercial ships through 'illegal passages'
The incident comes amid heightened regional uncertainty before Israeli elections and US midterms, with concerns about resumption of US-Israeli strikes on Iran

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed breakdown of the incident and Revolutionary Guard statements

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Emphasized electoral timing and diplomatic context, noting Iran remains open to talks

top_stories.headline: Russia Agrees 'In Principle' to Resume Ukraine Talks as Missiles Strike Kyiv
bullets: Russia said it is 'ready in principle' to resume trilateral peace talks with Ukraine and the US, following US envoy Steve Witkoff's meeting with Putin in St. Petersburg
Trump stated the world is 'the closest we've been' to ending the war, though Russia offered only technical-level talks in Abu Dhabi next month
Hours after the diplomatic announcements, missiles struck Kyiv, injuring at least six people and damaging houses
Putin's foreign policy aide indicated Witkoff brought no new proposals, and Russia showed little interest in a leaders' summit unless held in Moscow

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed diplomatic analysis, noting Russia sees 'little to talk about'

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Straightforward coverage of both sides' readiness to talk

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Emphasized continued attacks despite talk of negotiations

top_stories.headline: Nigeria Confirms Ebola Case in Capital as Outbreak Spreads Westward Across Africa
bullets: A woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for Ebola in Abuja after showing symptoms on October 7 and being hospitalized four days later
Nigerian authorities are tracing 44 contacts; Uganda's health ministry said the patient only transited through the country and had traveled to eastern Congo
Kenya confirmed its first case earlier this month and has since recorded nine infections; Africa CDC director called it 'an extremely serious threat'
The patient's nationality and travel timeline remain under investigation

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized regional spread and Africa CDC warnings about outbreak severity

top_stories.headline: International Criminal Court Awarded EU Sakharov Prize Amid US Sanctions Pressure
bullets: The International Criminal Court received the European Union's 2026 Sakharov Prize for human rights work
The award comes two weeks after Trump announced sanctions against the ICC and hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay received the Nobel Peace Prize
ICC President Tomoko Akane said the prize 'comes at a time when the court and its officials face unprecedented challenges'
The ICC has faced sustained pressure from the Trump administration since issuing arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and his former defense minister

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Framed as international rebuke of US pressure, noting Trump's threat to dismantle court 'brick by brick'
